indeterminate.finding: The create-payload translation forwards `priority` unchanged as a bare string (e.g. "Medium"), but Jira DC REST v2 requires priority as an object like {"name": "Medium"}. Since the DC create payload always carries `priority` as a bare string, this will 400 the create with the same 'cannot be set / unknown' error the fix set out to eliminate.
merged_from: The create translation forwards `assignee` (a bare or empty string) straight through as a Jira create field instead of routing it through the transport's `_assign` seam. An empty-string assignee is not an unassign for pycontribs/jira and a bare username is searched, not set — this is exactly the bug-751e hazard, which the update path deliberately handles via `_assign`.

The only empty-headline test sets BOTH title and summary empty, so a regression that failed to fall back from a blank title to the differ's summary (e.g. aborting the create instead) would not be detected.
merged_from: _create_issuetype's bare-string issuetype branch and the default 'Task' fallback are new branches with no test. Tests cover only ticket_type (bridge string) and dict-shaped issuetype; the `isinstance(jira_type, str)` path (line 88) and the terminal `{"name": "Task"}` default (line 90) are untested.

The description truncation (fit_outbound to WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT) introduced by this diff is untested: only a short pass-through description is asserted. Unlike the summary (which has an oversize-truncation test), an oversize description path has no coverage, so a regression removing or breaking the fit_outbound call would not be caught.

The diff's explicit non-allowlist design — passing through Jira-valid fields (priority, assignee, parent, labels, custom fields) untouched — is not asserted in this file. The docstrings state this is a deliberate choice to avoid silently dropping differ-emitted content, but no test feeds such a field through create_issue and asserts it reaches the client.
